purpose: Define explicit detection and reconciliation when source and destination/peer states diverge, forbidding silent newest-wins or arrival-order conflict resolution.

topics.name: DWH Replication Conflict Reconciliation
topics.purpose: Define explicit detection and reconciliation when source and destination/peer states diverge, forbidding silent newest-wins or arrival-order conflict resolution.

semantics.conflict_rule: Conflicts are detected using exact record identity, revision/version expectations and replication profile.
semantics.authority_rule: Authoritative-source policy, if used, is explicit per replication profile.
semantics.merge_rule: Semantic merge is a separate reconciliation operation with exact source states and provenance.
semantics.last_write_rule: Last-write-wins is forbidden unless explicitly declared with a trustworthy ordering source/profile.
semantics.time_rule: Local clocks/mtimes never decide conflict authority by themselves.
semantics.result_rule: Reconciliation produces an explicit accepted revision/state and records all contributing conflicting revisions.
semantics.history_rule: Losing/conflicting states remain traceable according to retention/audit policy.
semantics.failure_rule: Unresolvable conflict remains conflicted and does not silently advance the sync watermark.

invariants.rule: Replica/sync state, transport position or local copy never replaces the semantic identity or ownership of the authoritative source data; propagation is explicit, provenance-bearing and conflict-aware.

references.purpose: Replication conflicts reuse exact version conflict semantics.

prose.summary: Define explicit detection and reconciliation when source and destination/peer states diverge, forbidding silent newest-wins or arrival-order conflict resolution.
